title: 独自航海的少女与用脚听话的大象

blocks.en: Hello, young explorers, and welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening! Today we meet two great listeners: a teenage girl who sailed around the world all by herself, and the biggest land animal on Earth — an animal that listens with its feet! One teaches us courage; the other, the art of listening. Let's go!
blocks.title: 开场白
blocks.cn: 你好，小小探险家们，欢迎回到 Michael 的早听晚读！今天我们要认识两位了不起的“倾听者”：一位独自驾船环游世界的少女，和陆地上最大的动物——一种用脚来听远方朋友说话的动物。一个教我们勇气，一个教我们倾听的艺术。出发吧！

blocks.en: Laura Dekker was born on a boat, and she learned to sail as a small child. At fourteen, she told her parents her big dream: to sail around the world all alone. The grown-ups worried: the sea is huge, and storms do not care how old you are. But Laura did not give up. She learned to read maps and fix engines, and waited with patience.
blocks.title: 独自航海的少女
blocks.cn: 劳拉·德克出生在船上，从小就会开船。十四岁那年，她告诉爸爸妈妈自己的大梦想：一个人驾船环游世界。大人们都担心：大海那么大，暴风雨才不管你几岁。可劳拉没有放弃。她学会了看地图、修发动机，耐心地等待着，直到有人点头同意。

blocks.en: At last she set off in her vivid red boat, a twelve-metre ketch called Guppy. She steered through the Panama Canal, across the wide Pacific, and past sunny islands. Sea spray flew over the bow, and at night she slept in short naps, one ear open for the wind. Once, in the Indian Ocean, a great storm shook her boat for days, but Laura held on and sailed on.
blocks.title: 独自航海的少女
blocks.cn: 终于，她驾驶着鲜艳的红色小船出发了——那是一艘十二米长的双桅帆船，名叫“古比”。她穿过巴拿马运河，横渡宽阔的太平洋，经过阳光明媚的岛屿。海浪的水花飞过船头，夜里她只睡短短一会儿，一只耳朵还留意着风声。有一次，在印度洋上，一场大风暴摇晃了她的小船好几天，可劳拉坚持住了，继续航行。

blocks.en: After five hundred and eighteen days at sea, Laura sailed into Sint Maarten. Pedestrians on the shore stopped and cheered, and the whole harbour erupted in cheers. At sixteen, she was the youngest person ever to sail around the world alone. The caption under her photo says simply: a girl, a boat, and a dream. Today she is an ambassador for young sailors, teaching them to sail and to believe in themselves.
blocks.title: 独自航海的少女
blocks.cn: 在海上航行了五百一十八天后，劳拉驶入了圣马丁。岸边的行人们停下脚步，欢呼起来，整个港口都爆发出欢呼声。十六岁的她，成了有史以来独自驾船环游世界的最年轻的人。她照片下面的说明简单地写着：一个女孩，一艘船，一个梦想。如今，她是年轻水手的代言人，教他们开船、相信自己。

blocks.en: Now let's walk onto the land of Africa, where the biggest land animal on Earth is talking in a voice we can barely hear. An elephant's rumble is so low that it sits below what our ears can catch. To us, the elephant seems almost silent, and we are nearly deaf to its deepest calls. But other elephants, kilometres away, hear it clearly. Their message comes in more than one format: sound through the air, and trembles through the ground.
blocks.title: 用脚听话的大象
blocks.cn: 现在，让我们走到非洲的大地上，陆地上最大的动物正在用我们几乎听不见的声音说话。大象的低鸣声非常低，低到我们的耳朵捕捉不到。对我们来说，大象似乎几乎是安静的，我们几乎听不见它最深沉的叫声。可几公里外的其他大象却听得清清楚楚。它们的信息不止一种形式：有通过空气传播的声音，也有通过地面传播的震动。

blocks.en: How do they feel the tremble? Under an elephant's foot there is a soft pad, full of tiny sensors that pick up vibrations. The tremble travels up the bones of the leg and into the inner ear, where the brain reads it as sound. Scientists in Namibia watched elephants at a waterhole: when a faraway rumble shook the ground, they froze, lifted one foot, and turned towards the sound. They even show fine discrimination — they can tell a family member's rumble from a stranger's. So an elephant does not only listen with its ears. It listens with its feet, too.
blocks.title: 用脚听话的大象
blocks.cn: 它们是怎么感觉到震动的呢？大象的脚底有一块柔软的脚垫，里面布满了能感知震动的小感受器。震动沿着腿骨向上传到内耳，大脑就把它解读为声音。纳米比亚的科学家们在水塘边观察大象：当远方的低鸣震动地面时，大象们会停住，抬起一只脚，转向声音传来的方向。它们甚至能细致地分辨——能分出家人和陌生大象的低鸣声。所以，大象不只用耳朵听，它还用脚来听。

blocks.en: Here's today's idiom: 'through thick and thin.' It means staying with someone in good times and in bad times — through thick forests and thin paths. Laura and her little boat went through thick and thin together: sunny days and great storms. Here's an example: 'True friends stay together through thick and thin.' Who has stayed with you through thick and thin?
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 今天的俚语是“through thick and thin”（风雨同舟、不离不弃）。它的意思是无论顺境还是逆境都陪伴在某人身边——穿过茂密的森林和稀疏的小路。劳拉和她的小船一起风雨同舟：晴朗的日子和大风暴都一起经历过。举个例子：“真正的朋友会风雨同舟。”有谁一直风雨同舟地陪伴着你呢？

blocks.en: Let's think about our stories. Laura sailed alone for more than five hundred days, and an elephant can hear a friend kilometres away — through the ground! Two questions for you. First: what dream would you chase, even if grown-ups said it was too hard? Second: if you could talk through the ground like an elephant, what would you say? Talk about it with your family!
blocks.title: 结束语与互动问题
blocks.cn: 我们来想想今天的故事。劳拉独自航行了五百多天，大象能通过地面听到几公里外的朋友！现在，轮到回答两个问题。第一：如果你有一个梦想，即使大人们说太难了，你还会去追吗？第二：如果你能像大象一样通过地面说话，你想说什么？和家人聊聊吧！

blocks.en: That's all for today, young explorers. Be brave like Laura, and listen like an elephant. And remember: true friends stay together through thick and thin! See you tomorrow morning!
blocks.title: 告别
blocks.cn: 今天的节目就到这里啦，小小探险家们。像劳拉一样勇敢，像大象一样善于倾听。还要记住：真正的朋友会风雨同舟！明天早上见！

children.text: and 连接两个方向短语
：up the bones of the leg（沿着腿骨向上）和 into the inner ear（进入内耳）是同一动作 travels 的两段路程，and 把它们串成一条完整的路线——先上行、再进入。
：where = in the inner ear（在内耳里），修饰前面的 the inner ear，说明大脑是在哪里把震动解读为声音的。where 从句前面必须有一个表示地点的名词（这里是 ear），不能悬空。
：read 在这里不是“读书”，而是“解读、理解”；it 指前面的 tremble（震动）；as sound 说明解读的结果是“声音”。整句逻辑链：
震动上行 → 进入内耳 → 大脑在那里把它解读为声音
"At sixteen, she was the youngest person ever to sail around the world alone."
. The text says she set off in
. The text says the foot has
"a soft pad, full of tiny sensors that pick up vibrations."
"It means staying with someone in good times and in bad times."
D. Your own translations — there is no key for this part. Read your Chinese aloud and check that it sounds natural.
